title: Basis for the decision on findings F-1 to F-3 from record 0032
position: The three findings are accepted as accurate. They are not corrected here because each one asks what a required proof has to show, or whether an authorisation exists, and re-slice 0005 items 4 and 8 reserve both for the lead. Correcting them unilaterally would repeat exactly what F-2 objects to.

findings.summary: The redelivery case is green without a redelivery having happened. The TRX shows one delivery of three messages, completed after 15 s; there is no second delivery, no PRECONDITION_FAILED and no channel close. The _deliveries counter is incremented and never asserted on.
findings.developerNote: The counter was written to make the consumer hold the first delivery past the acknowledgement window. The finding is right that nothing asserts the outcome of that. What the spec should assert — a second delivery and its successful acknowledgement — is a change to what a required proof demonstrates, and the underlying question named in D2 of the previous round, whether a batch time limit above the acknowledgement window should be reconciled by the product, is still open and belongs to the lead.
findings.smallestCorrection: Assert at least two deliveries and the processed message set, or reopen the case.

findings.summary: Two test semantics decisions cite a product owner authorisation dated 2026-08-10 that exists nowhere in the hash-bound exchange. Between sequence 29 and the freeze at 30 there is no record at all.
findings.developerNote: The authorisation was given, but outside the chain, and I wrote it into the freeze prose instead of asking for it to be bound. That is the defect: a decision that only the developer asserts is not an authorisation. No rollback of the two test changes is needed, the binding is.
findings.smallestCorrection: Bind both decisions through the chain, or the lead records the actual decision as its own record.

findings.summary: The exclusive case asserts ConnectionException, which on that path can only come from the sixty second readiness timeout introduced in the same round. A broker-reported conflict would arrive as RabbitMqConnectionException and would fail the assertion. The 63 s duration in the TRX confirms it.
findings.developerNote: Accurate. The assertion observes the generic readiness bound, not the exclusivity conflict, and cannot tell a locked queue from any other slow endpoint. Observing the transport-reported conflict needs either the endpoint fault or the declare exception, which is a change to what the proof demonstrates and, depending on the route, to the transport.
findings.smallestCorrection: Observe the transport-reported conflict, or reopen the case.

consequenceIfReopened: Two of the five due cases would no longer count as closed, openDefects would not be 0, and the required RabbitMQ category would lose its closing effect for this order. The gate itself stays green; what changes is what it is allowed to prove.
